newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end down on profit-taking.

text.p: French shares finished more than one percent lower on Tuesday after investors took profits on last week's rise of over five percent.
Traders said weakness in bonds and the dollar ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday also encouraged sellers.
The market is divided over whether the FOMC policy-making body will raise the Fed funds interest rate by a quarter percentage point to 5.50 percent, or leave them unchanged.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 33.17 points or 1.19 percent at 2,751.11. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 37 at 2,743.
Volume was a heavy 8.09 billion francs, pushed up by block trades.

LVMH ended down 2.76 percent at 1,447 francs. The drinks and luxury goods group put out a statement saying the failure of its DFS unit to win two main concessions at Hong Kong's new airport would have a limited impact on DFS's Hong Kong business after the share price fell sharply.

Eurotunnel shed 1.54 percent to 6.40 francs. The French and British co-chairmen will meet French transport minister Bernard Pons this week following Monday's meeting with Britain's transport minister, John Prescott, who wants a review of the freight Shuttle wagon design.
Lafarge, down 0.85 percent at 397.20 francs, was busy with block trades changing hands.

CLF-Dexia France said after the close that new lending to local authorities totalled 29.75 billion francs in the first four months and was expected to hit 100 billion by the end of the year. The Franco-Belgian banking group closed down 0.74 percent at 536.
Pinault-Printemps-Redoute firmed 0.92 percent to 2,512. The retailer's La Redoute mail order unit bought Ellos Gruppen AB of Sweden.
